newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.KOREAN BOND YIELDS END UP AS LIQUIDITY TIGHTENS.
newsitem.headline: S.KOREAN BOND YIELDS END UP AS LIQUIDITY TIGHTENS.

text.p: Benchmark bond yields ended sharply higher on Tuesday as the short-term liquidity tightened after financial institutions paid back loans owed to the government, dealers said.
The liquidity tightened even despite the central bank's supply of one trillion won in emergency funds, they said.
* 3-yr corporates close at 12.10 pct vs Monday's 12.00
* Overnight average call rate at 12.40 pct vs 12.17

"There were also fears that the year-on-year money supply had grown sharply so far and that this would force the central bank to keep its tight monetary policies," said Lim Kwang-taek of Korea Long-Term Credit Bank.
Dealers said three-year bond yields were expected to remain relatively high for the time being.
